why: Copying .env.example still leaves people stuck if they do not know what each variable does or which ones are optional. A clear table tells them what to fill in and where to get it.
question: What do these environment variables do, and where do I get them?

parts.heading: Variable table
parts.text: Use a table to list each variable's name, whether it is required, what it does, and where to get it (or its default). Every item in .env.example must be in this table.
parts.emphasis: Never paste real keys or passwords into the README or .env.example.

parts.heading: Note on browser-exposed variables
parts.text: In frontend projects, variables starting with VITE_ or NEXT_PUBLIC_ are bundled into the browser code. Remind readers never to put secret keys in them.

notes.title: Says "configure .env yourself"
notes.text: Readers cannot guess; list each variable in a table.

notes.title: Missing .env.example variables
notes.text: The example file has two variables; only one is here.

notes.title: Pasted a real key
notes.text: Anything in a README is public; revoke and rotate it.

lines: | Name | Required | Purpose | Where to get it |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | Yes | Order API URL | The shop |
`VITE_` variables end up in the browser; no secrets.

tip.title: Deleting a leaked key from the file is not enough
paragraphs: Once a real key is committed and pushed to GitHub, it stays in the commit history even if you delete the line in a later commit.
If a key ever slips in, go straight to that service's dashboard, revoke the exposed key, and generate a new one.

types.web-app: Point out which variables are bundled into the browser so nobody puts server secrets in them.
types.course-example: Make the defaults work out of the box right after copying; if an API key is required, walk through getting a free one.
types.portfolio: Interviewers will not sign up for third-party keys just to test your app—make it run with default values whenever possible.
types.backend-api: List database URLs, auth secrets, and third-party keys in full, and note which ones must be set before the server can start.
